mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals a consumption contraction with offsetting housing demand, resulting in flat equity valuations and near-zero S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST > previous 6-month average
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are significantly positive or negative (t-test p < 0.05) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressure and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of three consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of higher inflation and tighter policy, which increases uncertainty and risk premia, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS exceed their 12-month moving averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) below its 6-month moving average, combined with a stable unemployment rate, signals weakening consumer demand without labor market distress, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 6-mo MA AND UNRATE within ±0.2pp of previous month for 3 months
regime_hint: consumer demand weakening, stable labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months with RSAFS below its 6-month moving average and stable unemployment.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of two consecutive months with PAYEMS growth above 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the housing starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a prolonged housing downturn, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-mo MA for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of four consecutive months with HOUST below its 12-month moving average.
